newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open down 5.00 to 6.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open down 5.00 to 6.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 5.00 to 6.00 cents lower Friday after a weak showing in London overnight, floor sources said.
LIFFE coffee futures erased early gains and traded sharply lower at midday Friday, pressured by commercial selling. May was off $24 at $1,585 a tonne. July fell $14 to $1,630.
But labor unrest in Colombia and continued supply concerns should provide underlying support, traders said.
Strike negotiators in Colombia said that talks aimed at ending a six-day-old work stoppage by truckers continued Friday morning, but a key union demand remained unresolved.

They said about 18 points on the list of demands put forward by the truckers union had been settled, bBut there was still no agreement over the union's demand for the government to set minimum cargo rates for highway freight.

On Thursday, New York arabica futures closed sharply higher bolstered by speculative after after a Colombian coffee official said a strike by the country's main trucker drivers' union could delay exports of up to 200,000 70-kg bags of coffee this week and may cause serious problems meeting May export commitments.

Most-active July futures rose 4.80 cents a lb on the day, to 198.20, having traded from 185.50 to 196 cents. Spot May gained 3.10, to finish at 214.30, while the outer months gained between 0.05 and 5.00 cents.
Technically, traders pegged July support at 192.50 cents, while resistance was seen at 199.00 cents, a contract high set on Monday, and 200.00 cents.
"After yesterday, I thought we would open 2.00 to 3.00 higher today," one trader said. "But I think if (July) fails at 200.00 again, we're probably going to drop."
After Thursday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 6,250 60-kg bags, to 50,350 bags as of April 23. There were 815 bags of coffee pending certification, the exchange said.
